what: MEASURED 2026-09-22T13:13Z by the E20 lane, by CREATING the Routine and FIRING it once rather than assuming it worked. E20 asked for the lane-reconcile invariant enforced 'somewhere involuntary', because a Routine firing into the MANAGER's session is a reminder a manager can skip -- reason (5), the one that killed DUE.md. The design chosen was a Routine firing into a FRESH session (create_new_session_on_fire), so the manager is not in the path. [!] IT DOES NOT WORK, AND THE FIRING IS WHAT ESTABLISHED THAT. `create_trigger` returned a warning in terms: 'this trigger stores no MCP connectors, so the sessions it fires will run without connector (mcp__*) tools' -- so the fired session cannot call list_sessions, which is the watchdog's entire basis. Worse, get_session on the fired session (session_01GyB7Zej9GgVoodnfKz4Re5) shows its `session_context` carries NO `sources` at all, so it has no checkout of this repo and cannot run scripts/ops/lane_reconcile.py either. It was also served claude-sonnet-5 rather than the claude-haiku-4-5 passed at creation. [!] THE ABSENCE IS A REAL READING, NOT A GAP IN THE PROJECTION: get_session on an ordinary lane DOES return sources: [{git_repository: ...}] -- checked against this session's own record in the same minute -- so the field is emitted when there is a source, and two independent signals agree (the trigger's stored session_request.config.sources is also []). [!] THE ROUTINE IS THEREFORE DISABLED (trig_01MFG5cYsTsS1bci279A2TKi, renamed to say why), NOT LEFT RUNNING. A watcher that fires every six hours, cannot reach its subject and reports nothing is exactly the defect class E20 is about -- a check whose subject it cannot see, still counted as coverage -- and it would bill a session per firing to produce it. Leaving it enabled would be worse than not having it, and reporting 'the watchdog is in place' would have been the same false claim one level up. [!] SO THE INVARIANT IS STILL VOLUNTARY. What stands instead: .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md now requires `python3 scripts/ops/lane_reconcile.py --sessions <dump>` at every manager check-in, which is a discipline and not a mechanism, and is said that way. [!] WHAT ONLY A HUMAN CAN DO, and why: connectors on a Routine created through create_trigger are limited to those the calling session can pass through, and this session had none to pass. So the operator must open the Routines UI on claude.ai, attach the Claude Code Remote connector AND this repository as a source to `lane-watchdog`, re-enable it, and fire it once to confirm the fired session reports a reconciliation or an explicit could-not-look. Owner class: defaulted_to_human only in the sense that no wire exists from a session; the grant itself is genuinely a human action at the account level. Full write-up and the two cheaper designs that were measured and killed first: docs/claude/work/LANE-WATCHDOG-PROMPT.md.
